deep.reconstruction:
OVERALL: The page builds a table of DECADIC (10-adic) logarithms, i.e. Z_2 x Z_5 logarithms, of small integers. Most values are taken modulo 10^14, and log 1001 is taken modulo 10^15. Each one comes from the power series log(1+x) = sum (-1)^(k+1) x^k/k. In it, 1/k is read as an inverse modulo powers of 10 wherever gcd(k,10)=1, for example 1/3 = ...6667, 1/7 = ...2857143, 1/9 = ...88889, 1/11 = ...091. The previous page counts primes per hundred, so it is unrelated. The next page continues with multiples of log 1001 (866416999 501, 862918998 501, ...) and with series terms.

(A) Top left: idempotent / CRT decomposition modulo 10^5.
- '9 = 5^inf + 2^inf' means 9 = 15625 + 84384 (mod 10^5). Here 15625 is 0 mod 5^5 and 9 mod 2^5, while 84384 is 0 mod 2^5 and 9 mod 5^5.
- Equivalently 15625 = 9*e5 and 84384 = 9*e2 mod 10^5, with the decadic idempotents e5 = ...90625 and e2 = ...09376.
- '2a = 5^inf + 1' gives a = (15625+1)/2 = 7813, which is 1/2 modulo 5^6. 7813 appears at upper right. The line '5a/a = 2^inf+1' is presumably the analogous inverse of 5 modulo a power of 2.
- The other scratch numbers at upper right (1.1.2.1.2, 7182060, 15626, 71876, 34376, 82969, ...) I cannot reconstruct with certainty.

(B) Torsion splitting (left table). Every decadic unit is u = zeta*v. Here zeta lies in the 8-element torsion group {+-1} x mu_4, and v = 1 mod 20 (that is, v in 1+4Z_2 in the 2-part and 1+5Z_5 in the 5-part). The page defines log u := log v.
- Gauss uses epsilon = ...5807. It is -1 in Z_2 and a primitive 4th root of unity in Z_5, so epsilon^4 = 1.
- Then epsilon^2 = ...1249 (more fully ...81249: 1 mod 2^k, -1 mod 5^k), -epsilon^2 = ...18751, epsilon^3 = ...2943, -epsilon = ...4193.
- The rows 'n x m' give a multiplier m with n*m = 1 mod 20, making n*m a principal unit:
  - 1, 21 and 81 take m = 1;
  - 11 takes -epsilon^2 = 18751;
  - 9 takes epsilon^2 = (8)1249;
  - 3 takes epsilon = ...75807;
  - 7 takes epsilon^3 = ...992943;
  - 17 takes -epsilon = ...24193;
  - 13 is left blank.
- The ten-digit column holds the last ten digits of the logs: 1 -> 0; 11 -> 2750684460; 21 -> 3829935820; 81 -> 1146220880; 9 -> 8557310440; 3 -> 2786555220; 7 -> 9551280600; 17 -> ...5656080; 13 -> 4697535940.
- 'Numerus cuius L = 20 fit ...56568221' means: the number whose logarithm is 20 ends in ...56568221. This is presumably exp(20) = sum 20^k/k!, which converges decadically. It ends in 21, consistent with being 1 mod 20. I have not verified the digits.

(C) log 11 = log(1+10), mod 10^14.
- Odd terms: 10 + 10^3/3 (66666666667000) + 10^5/5 (20000) + 10^7/7 (2857 14300 00000) + 10^9/9 (88889*10^9) + 10^11/11 (091*10^11) + 10^13/13 (7*10^13). The sum is 6322 70966 87010.
- Even terms: 10^2/2 = 50, 10^4/4 = 2500, 10^6/6 = 3333 33335 00000, 10^8/8 = 125 00000, 10^10/10 = 10^9, 10^12/12 = 6675*10^10, 10^14/14 = 5*10^13, 10^16/16 = 25*10^12. The sum is 7508 43460 02550.
- Difference: log 11 = 8814 27506 84460 (mod 10^14).
- Since log(-1) = 0 in Z_2, this equals log(11*(-epsilon^2)) for the torsion-free part.

(D) log 9 and log 3.
- My reconstruction: log 99 = log(1-100) = -sum 100^k/k = ...49831307994900 (mod 10^14).
- On the page: log 9 = log 99 - log 11 = 6168 85573 10440. The line 3831 14426 89560 is -log 9 (mod 10^14).
- log 3 = log 9 / 2. Halving is ambiguous by 5*10^13, so Gauss writes the leading digit stacked as 3 or 8: log 3 = (3|8)084 42786 55220.

(E) log 1001, mod 10^15, with x = 1000.
- x + x^3/3 + x^5/5 = 86666 70000 01000.
- x^2/2 + x^4/4 = 25 00005 00000.
- log 1001 = 86641 69995 01000, exact as checked.
- Similarly log(1/999) = x + x^2/2 + x^3/3 + x^4/4 + x^5/5 = 86691 70005 01000, so log 999 = 13308 29994 99000.
- The line '666999 501 000 | 1001' is an earlier, incomplete approximation of log 1001 modulo 10^12.

(F) Deductions from factorisations, all mod 10^14.
- 1001 = 7*11*13: log 1001 - log 11 = 7827 42488 16540 = log 91.
- log 13 = log 91 - log 7 = (7|2)303 46975 35940.
- 999 = 27*37: log 27 = 3 log 3 = (9|4)253 28359 65660.
- log 37 = log 999 - log 27 = (4|9)055 01635 33340.
- The torsion parts cancel because 1001 = 1 (mod 20) and 999 = 19 (mod 20); torsion -1 has log 0.

(G) log 21 = log(1+20) and log 19 = log(1-20).
- Odd terms: 20 + 20^3/3 = 3333 33333 36000 (written with 20 and the 64 of 20^5/5 = 64*10^5) + 20^7/7 = 5714 30400... + 20^9/9 (1116 8...) + 20^11/11 (368...) + 20^13/13 (4...). The sum S_odd is 7844 43739 76020.
- Even terms: 200 + 40000 + 20^6/6 (3333 33440...) + 20^8/8 (32000...) + 20^10/10 (0102 4...) + 20^12/12 (0800...). The sum S_even is 4236 05440 40200.
- log 21 = S_odd - S_even = 3608 38299 35820.
- log 7 = log 21 - log 3 = (0|5)523 95512 80600.
- log 19 = log(-19) = log(1-20) = -(S_odd + S_even) = -(1)2080 49180 16220 = 7919 50819 83780.

(H) Right-hand list 0001, 1001, ..., 9001, 0101, ..., 9101: a planned argument list for a logarithm table (numbers 1 mod 100, or their endings).

The purpose is evidently a decadic analogue of a logarithm table, an additive 'index' calculus modulo 10^n. All logs are determined modulo 10^14, up to the 5*10^13 halving ambiguity.
errors: The line '666999 501 000 | 1001' gives log 1001 mod 10^12 as 666999501000. It omits the -x^4/4 = -2.5*10^11 term; the correct residue is 416999501000. The right-hand column later supplies the 25 00005 00000 correction, giving the exact 86641 69995 01000.

Not an error, but worth noting: the leading digits of log 3, 7, 13, 27, 37 are written stacked (3|8, 0|5, 7|2, 9|4, 4|9). This correctly reflects that halving modulo 10^14 is determined only up to 5*10^13.

Every value checked by hand (log 1001, log 999, log 99, log 11 via both routes, log 9, log 3, log 27, log 37, log 91, log 13, log 21, log 7, log 19, the epsilon powers, the idempotent split of 9) is arithmetically consistent. No slips found apart from the first item.

results.what: Decadic (10-adic) logarithm log(1+x) = sum (-1)^(k+1) x^k/k, evaluated modulo 10^14 to 10^15 for x = 10, 20, -20, -100, 1000, -1000, with 1/k interpreted as a 10-adic inverse
results.modern_name: p-adic / g-adic logarithm (Z_10 = Z_2 x Z_5)
results.usually_credited_to: K. Hensel (p-adic numbers 1897; p-adic log/exp in Theorie der algebraischen Zahlen, 1908)

results.what: Splitting each decadic unit into a torsion part in {+-1} x mu_4, using epsilon = ...5807 with epsilon^4 = 1 and epsilon^2 = ...81249, times a principal unit 1 mod 20; logs are defined on the principal part
results.modern_name: Structure of Z_10^*: mu x (1+4Z_2) x (1+5Z_5); Teichmüller decomposition
results.usually_credited_to: Hensel; Teichmüller (1936) for the systematic representatives

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an unambiguous, correct computation of 10-adic logarithms by power series with 10-adic inverses of denominators. It combines this with an explicit torsion/principal-unit splitting (a 4th root of unity epsilon in the 5-part, -1 in the 2-part) and builds a log table from factorisations. This is Hensel's p-adic logarithm in all but name, decades earlier. Gauss's index calculus and moduli-2^n work are known, and this may be partly noted in Nachlass literature I am unsure of. So I rate it notable rather than revolutionary.

checkable.asserts: epsilon = ...5807 is a 4th root of unity mod 10^4 with the stated powers

The multiplier for 9 is (8)1249 = epsilon^2; for 3 it is ...75807 = epsilon.
Leading digits are written stacked as alternatives: log 3 = 3|8 084..., log 7 = 0|5 523..., log 13 = 7|2 303..., log 27 = 9|4 253..., log 37 = 4|9 055....
The right-column label 'log 1001' applies to 86641 69995 01000. The following entries are log 11, log 91 (7827 42488 16540), log 7, log 13, log 1/999, log 999, log 27, log 37.
In the log 21 block, '20' and '64' are the terms 20 and 20^5/5 = 64*10^5 added to 20^3/3.
